Q: Difference between llm and chat llm in langchain A:

Yes, this is expected behavior in LangChain.

When using a chain like LLMChain or a RunnableSequence, a ChatPromptTemplate can format a list of messages into a single prompt string before passing it to the LLM. The chain's input schema is flexible—it accepts messages if the prompt supports them—but the LLM itself receives a string, so no schema error occurs on the model side.​​

The LLM outputs a plain string, unlike ChatModels' AIMessage object with metadata (e.g., tool calls). This is why you notice the output difference; inputs "work" due to chain/prompt conversion, but direct LLM invocation with messages would fail. For chat apps, prefer ChatModels to avoid manual string formatting.

Q: run script if Date_1 > Date_2 A:

When I saw your sample Spreadsheet, I confirmed that the value of New and Old are the string values like 31/03/2021 and 31/12/2020. If your actual situation is the same with this sample Spreadsheet, from this situation, when you want to compare New > Old, I would like to propose to convert the string value to the date object. By this, New > Old can be used. And, when the values of New and Old are retrieved by one request, I thought that the process cost will become a bit low. When these points are reflected to your script, it becomes as follows.

Modified script:

Please modify your script as follows.

From:

const New = SS.getRange('B1').getValue();
const Old = SS.getRange('C1').getValue();

To:

const values = SS.getRange('B1:C1').getValues()[0];
const [[NewD, NewM, NewY], [OldD, OldM, OldY]] = values.map(v => v ? v.split("/") : Array(3).fill(""));
const New = NewD && NewM && NewY ? new Date(NewY, NewM - 1, NewD).getTime() : "";
const Old = OldD && OldM && OldY ? new Date(OldY, OldM - 1, OldD).getTime() : "";

Note:

  • If at your actual situation, the values of New and Old are the date object, you can also the following modification.

    • From

        const New = SS.getRange('B1').getValue();
  const Old = SS.getRange('C1').getValue();

    • To

        const values = SS.getRange('B1:C1').getValues()[0];
  const [New, Old] = values.map(v => v ? v.getTime() : "");

References:

  • map()
  • Date()

Q: Why is gunicorn not being added to path in an AWS App Runner Flask App? A:

If you are deploying a Python Flask Application on Aws App Runner using source github/bitbucket repository , you may see errors like:

  • no module named gunicorn

  • exec: "gunicorn": executable file is not found in $PATH

This happens because when using source code deployment , App runner installs dependencies in a location that is not automatically added to the runtime PATH.

A Working solution is to install the dependencies into the application directory itself using the --target option.

Build Command

pip3 install -r requirements.txt --target .

Start Command

python3 -m gunicorn -b 0.0.0.0:8080 app:app

After spending couple of hours troubleshooting, I found that installing the dependencies using the --target . option resolved the errors above mentioned.
